This Ember RV Travel Trailer Can Turn Its Bunk Room Into a Mobile Office or Cargo Space
16 photos
Photo: Ember RV/ That RV Girl
No two RV trips are the same, and that is why flexibility is an important aspect when choosing a travel trailer. One weekend might be about family time, the next could be about outdoor adventures, while another might call for a designated workspace on the road. A travel trailer with a fixed floor plan might feel too rigid when your adventure needs change.
That’s why travelers are now looking for RVs that can adapt to their traveling plans. Ember RV understands this need for increased flexibility on the road and has introduced a new travel trailer that can do more than one thing. Meet the Touring Edition 2850DBL, a travel trailer that integrates the manufacturer’s exclusive EmberTrack E-track system that has versatility written all over it.
The EmberTrack E-track is a really interesting configurable setup that allows owners to transform the rear section of the RV into whatever you need, from storage space to bunk room, workspace, or an open cargo area. This versatility lets you transform the unit from a couple’s travel trailer to one suitable for family camping or for working on the road.
Ember RV’s Touring Edition is a premium travel trailer lineup aimed at RVers who want an elevated camping experience, with more comfort, durable construction, refined finishes, and confident towing for anything from weekend adventures to longer trips.
Photo: Ember RV/ That RV Girl The new 2850DBL is a two-axle model with one slide-out and a rare two-door floor plan. The main entry door opens into the living area, while the secondary one enters the private front master suite. The towable RV measures 32 feet and 11 inches (10 meters) in overall length, but it feels more spacious than its footprint thanks to that slide-out and its 8-foot (2.4-meter) width.
Like all the models in the Touring Edition lineup, this model is built with laminated aluminum-framed construction, Azdel Onboard composite exterior walls with gel-coated fiberglass finish, and a fully walkable roof covered in one-piece Tufflex PVC roofing. It rides on aluminum rims with Goodyear Endurance tires and a CURT Touring Coil Suspension system with heavy-duty coil springs and shock absorbers on each wheel, which is meant to make towing smoother.
The 2850DBL is one of those RVs that provide residential comfort inside but also encourage outdoor living . It features a 20-foot (6-meter) power awning that creates a large shaded area beside the trailer. Underneath, there is a clever fold-up “Bar-V” window and a fold-down table, creating a connection between the interior living area and the outside campsite. It can also be closed off with an integrated screen or shade.
Photo: Ember RV/ That RV Girl The exterior station includes a TV, a bar section, standard outlets, and plenty of space to put an induction stove for cooking if needed, creating a great setup for outdoor cooking, camp-day cocktails, tailgating or watching a game outside.
However, the feature that really sets this model apart is the EmberTrack E-track system at the rear. Another fold-up window and fold-down bartop open to reveal a generous open space that can be configured as you please. From the factory, this space comes equipped with two double-over-double bunk beds, but these aren’t permanent installations. They’re mounted on E-track rails, allowing for plenty of flexibility .
Photo: Ember RV/ That RV Girl Owners can opt for a single-over-double arrangement or individual single bunks, or position the bed bases so that they can create shelves or a desktop, turning this rear area into a mobile workspace. The beds can also be mounted on an upper position or removed altogether to free up cargo space for hauling e-bikes, dog kennels, outdoor gear, and more. You can even hang a hammock in this space and chill out while enjoying the breeze. A large baggage door at the rear makes getting larger things inside easier.
Other exterior features include a pass-through storage compartment at the front and a tongue gear box with two compartments - one for two propane bottles and one for tools.
As for the interior arrangement, the 2850DBL floor plan comprises a private front bedroom, a central living and cooking area, plus a bathroom and the repositionable EmberTrack bunk/storage system at the rear.
Photo: Ember RV/ That RV Girl The slide-out adds extra width to the living area and houses theater seating with three recliners and rotating side tables, a 12-cubic-foot 12V French-door refrigerator, and a floor-to-ceiling pantry. Across the living area, there is what the manufacturer calls the “EmberFlex Dinesk,” a long bar table that can be configured as a dining table, a bar, or a desktop, depending on what you actually need. It connects to the outdoor fold-down bartop and a dining table slides from underneath it when you need space for more people to sit down and enjoy a meal together.
The kitchen comes with solid-surface countertops, base and upper cabinets, an undermount stainless steel sink, and a flip-up counter extension. The appliance package includes the aforementioned fridge, a cast-iron three-burner cooktop, and an over-the-range convection microwave/air fryer. There is also a coffee bar next to the sofa, with a small counter space and storage.
Photo: Ember RV/ That RV Girl The front bedroom is fully enclosed and fitted with a walk-around residential queen bed measuring 60 by 80 inches (152 by 203 cm). The bed has integrated storage underneath, but it’s also flanked by two wardrobes. Practical nightstand cubbies with outlets are integrated on either side of the bed, and there is also TV prep on the opposite wall. Apart from the “real queen” bed, the nicest feature is that the bedroom has its own entry door for direct access from the outside.
The bathroom inside this RV is compact but so well designed that it feels residential. It includes a large shower with sliding door, a nice size vanity, a corner medicine cabinet, a toilet, and even additional storage cubbies.
Ember RV has also equipped this new travel trailer with the systems needed for extended off-grid adventures. The mandatory Off-Grid Solar Package gives you 400 watts of rooftop solar panels, a 2,000-watt inverter, and a Victron MPPT solar controller. The 2850DBL also carries 55 gallons (208 liters) of freshwater, while the gray and black water tanks hold 70 and 35 gallons (265 and 132 liters), respectively.
Other standard features include a HD television, two Furrion Chill Cube AC units with heat pumps, the EmberLink smart RV system, a 12V Multi-speed Fan, and a 30K BTU furnace.
The Ember RV Touring Edition 2850DBL has a dry weight of 7,395 pounds (3,354 kg), a gross vehicle weight of 9,495 pounds (4,306 kg), which leaves it with a cargo carrying capacity of 2,100 pounds (952 kg). Pricing for this travel trailer starts at $78,355.
